selected_layer: compiler_resource_budget (UB tiling geometry) - keep the tile+GLOBAL GROUP pipelining hypothesis, shrink the tile so automatic multi-buffering fits the 192 KiB AIV UB
layer_reason: The failure stage is BiShengHIR resource allocation, not numerics: the diagnostic requires 1841152 bits and the source accounting reproduces exactly 12*16384 + 2*16384 + 768 B = 1841152 bits for the 128x64 bf16 tile, so the excess comes only from the tile byte budget multiplied by the compiler's multi-buffering of the six in-flight tiles. Changing index arithmetic or masks cannot reduce it; only the tile geometry can.
simulator_incremental_judgment: No current-source simulator or profiling evidence is available for this repair; existing simulator-evidence.json and current-profiling.json describe earlier sources and are treated as historical background only, not as causal evidence for this change. Judgment for this edit therefore rests on the compiler diagnostic plus the exact byte accounting, and the next paired profiling run must re-establish any performance claim.
diagnostic: loc(candidate.py:39:0): error: ub overflow, requires 1841152 bits while 1572864 bits available! (possible reason: tiling basic block is too large or block number is more than what user expect due to multi-buffer feature is enabled and some ops need extra local buffer.) -> error: Failed to run BiShengHIR pipeline; bishengir-compile exited with status 1 under --enable-auto-multi-buffer=True

evidence.finding: Preflight of sha 4bfa839d failed at compile: ub overflow, 1841152 bits required vs 1572864 available (192 KiB AIV UB); no numerical or device result exists for this source.

Full compiler log: the traceback ends in subprocess.CalledProcessError from /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.0.0/bin/bishengir-compile (linalg-to-npu-binary stage), so the failure is a UB resource allocation inside BiShengHIR, not a Triton frontend, indexing or numerical error. The same UB message repeats for each oversized compilation variant.

Actual pre-compile IR of the failing variant: tt.make_range end=128 (BLOCK_S) and end=64 (BLOCK_D) with bf16 pointers, i.e. one tile = 8192 elements = 16384 bytes for the large two-byte cases ([8,512,3072], head_dim 64). The small-tile variants in the same directory (8x16, 32x16) are orders of magnitude below UB and are not the reported overflow.

Source accounting reproduces the reported bit count exactly for T=16384 B: the pipelined GROUP loop (tl.range num_stages=2) makes the compiler double-buffer the six in-flight tiles (q,k,v in plus q,k,v out) = 12*T = 196608 B, plus the float32 upcast tile of the q path (2*T = 32768 B, required so fp16/bfloat16 cannot overflow before the 1/sqrt(head_dim) rescale) plus three f32 bias vectors (3*64*4 = 768 B); 196608+32768+768 = 230144 B = 1841152 bits.

Two earlier attempts of this campaign failed the same UB check at 2146304 bits (268288 B) with still larger tiles, while qualified attempts 002/003 reached 0.0794 ms and 0.0635 ms, so smaller tile geometry is known to compile on this device.

hypothesis: The performance hypothesis (one program owns a [BLOCK_S, BLOCK_D] tile and walks GROUP consecutive seq blocks in a 2-stage loop so the next tile's MTE2 overlaps the current tile's vector/store) is sound; only the tile geometry exceeds the 192 KiB AIV UB once automatic multi-buffering is applied. Fitting the same pipeline needs 12*T + 2*T + 768 <= 196608 B, i.e. T <= 14043 B, and tile extents must be powers of two, so the largest fitting tile is 8192 bytes (BLOCK_S halved for the wide-head cases).
change: Focused single-mechanism edit: _TILE_BYTES 16384 -> 8192, with the comment updated to record the measured UB accounting. Indexing, the EXACT and masked paths, the GROUP=2 pipelined loop, fp32 bias-add/rescale opmath and generic strides are untouched; the only other effect is that block_s halves wherever the seq_len cap does not bind, so the grid doubles and each program still walks GROUP=2 tiles with num_stages=2.
expected: Compilation succeeds with a predicted UB request of 12*8192 + 16384 + 768 = 115456 B (59% of the 196608 B budget, 1.7x margin), leaving room for the extra local buffers the diagnostic mentions. Small shapes whose block_s is capped by seq_len keep their previous geometry and behaviour. Numerics unchanged: bias add and rescale stay in float32 with a single rounding to the output dtype. Performance should stay close to the pipelined hypothesis; the doubled program count on the large cases is the cost to be measured.
validation: 1) Record this diagnosis through the decision bridge before editing. 2) Preflight the new candidate: compilation must finish without any ub overflow, and every correctness check must pass, exercising both the EXACT and the masked path and the fp32 opmath path. 3) Then collect paired profiling/simulator evidence on transform_bias_rescale_qkv-timing-2 to test whether the GROUP pipelining still pays at the halved tile; tune GROUP or the per-path tile if it does not.
unknown: Whether the allocator double-buffers exactly the six tile buffers plus the fp32 intermediate; the byte count matches exactly, but the allocator model is not directly observable.
Whether halving the tile loses more per-program DMA/launch overhead than the still-pipelined GROUP loop recovers; only paired profiling can decide.

Why small-tile (8x16, 32x16) variants also appear in failed-ir; their UB footprint is tiny, so they are assumed to be IR dumps of the same aborted run rather than independent failures. Preflight must confirm they still pass.
